presets.title: Audit DataTables for missing and suspicious rows
presets.summary: Read the selected DataTables' rows and values, flag empty, zero and duplicate-looking entries, and prove the snapshot complete. Read-only.

placeholders.name: rules
placeholders.label: Rules to check
placeholders.default: every number above 0; no empty text or name; no missing asset reference

presets.prompt:
Audit these DataTables without changing them: {{selected_assets}}.
1. hyper_data_inspect with those object paths as targetPaths (load any table that reports asset_not_loaded with Epic's AssetTools load_asset, then inspect again): each table's row struct and row names.
2. hyper_data_validate with the full, unpaged Snapshot: it must be valid and complete; report any issue codes.
3. Epic's DataTableTools get_schema and get_rows for every row. Check: {{rules}}; row names follow one pattern; no two rows are identical apart from their name.
4. Report a table per DataTable: row | column | value | rule | PASS/WARN/FAIL, then totals per table. Suggest fixes, but make none and save nothing.

presets.title: Build an item DataTable from a new struct and enum
presets.summary: Make an item-type enum and an item row struct, create a DataTable on them with starter rows, and prove fields, values and row count.

placeholders.name: rows
placeholders.label: Starter rows
placeholders.default: Sword_Iron (Weapon, 120 gold, 3.5 kg), Potion_Health (Consumable, 25 gold, 0.3 kg), Shield_Oak (Armor, 80 gold, 4 kg)

presets.prompt:
Under {{content_folder}}/Data, create the item data for {{project}}. If the blueprint_structure pack is unavailable, say so and stop.
1. hyper_data_inspect on {{content_folder}}/Data/E_ItemType, S_ItemRow and {{table_name}}: each must report does_not_exist; otherwise stop and ask.
2. One hyper_blueprint_structure_apply_plan (fresh OperationId, bSave false, no BlueprintPath): `enum.create` {{content_folder}}/Data/E_ItemType with Values {{item_types}}; then `struct.create` {{content_folder}}/Data/S_ItemRow with Fields DisplayName (text), Type (enum: the new enum's path), Price (int, 0), Weight (float, 0) and Icon (object:/Script/Engine.Texture2D), each with a tooltip. hyper_operation_wait if it waits for approval.
3. Epic's DataTableTools: create {{table_name}} on S_ItemRow, add_rows, then set_rows with the column keys get_schema returns, for: {{rows}}.
4. hyper_data_inspect on all three (load any that report asset_not_loaded) and hyper_data_validate on the full Snapshot.
5. Report a PASS/FAIL table: enum values in order, struct fields with types, row count, and each row's values from get_rows. Leave the assets unsaved unless I ask.

presets.title: Rename a struct field safely across the project
presets.summary: Rename one field of a user-defined struct through a checked, hash-sealed plan, then prove the struct and the Blueprints using it still load clean.
presets.prompt:
In {{selected_asset}}, rename field `{{old_field}}` to `{{new_field}}`; change nothing else.
1. hyper_data_inspect with targetPaths [{{selected_asset}}] (load it first with Epic's AssetTools load_asset if it reports asset_not_loaded): the field's StableId (its GUID), its ElementFingerprint and the snapshot's PersistedFingerprint. If `{{new_field}}` already exists, stop.
2. hyper_asset_dependency_graph with direction referencers and maxDepth 1: the Blueprints and DataTables that use the struct.
3. hyper_data_apply_plan with bDryRun true, TargetPath the struct, ExpectedPersistedFingerprint, and one op `user_struct.rename_field` (SubjectId the GUID, ExpectedElementFingerprint, Name {{new_field}}). Then the same request with bDryRun false, a fresh OperationId and ExpectedPlanHash set to its PlanHash. If it is refused (Strict Safety), quote the reason and stop.
4. hyper_data_inspect again and hyper_data_validate on the full Snapshot: the field reads `{{new_field}}` with the same GUID and type. hyper_diagnose with checks loaded_blueprint_health for the referencers (load them with Epic's AssetTools load_asset first).
5. Report a PASS/FAIL table: renamed, same GUID and type, snapshot valid, each referencer healthy. The plan saves the struct; say so.

presets.title: Rebalance a level-up curve in a CurveTable
presets.summary: Rewrite one CurveTable row's keys from a formula, keep it rising level to level, and prove the key count, range and values against the spec.
presets.prompt:
In {{selected_asset}}, rewrite row `{{row}}` so the key at level L has value {{formula}}, for levels {{levels}}.
1. hyper_data_inspect on it (load it first with Epic's AssetTools load_asset if it reports asset_not_loaded): every row's key count, time range, default value and ElementFingerprint. Epic's CurveTableTools get_keys for {{row}}: put the old keys in your reply as the undo record.
2. Compute the new keys; each must be higher than the one before. Show the first 5 and the last 5 before writing.
3. Epic's CurveTableTools set_keys for {{row}} only (time = level, value = result); touch no other row.
4. hyper_data_inspect again and hyper_data_validate on the full Snapshot: {{row}}'s key count and time range match {{levels}}; every other row's ElementFingerprint is unchanged. get_keys for {{row}} again: every key equals the computed value.
5. Report a table: level | old | new | PASS/FAIL (rises, matches the formula), then the totals. Leave the asset unsaved unless I ask.

presets.title: Collect UI strings into a localizable String Table
presets.summary: Create a String Table with stable keys for a screen's text, verify its id, namespace and keys, and say how each key is referenced.

placeholders.name: entries
placeholders.label: Key = text entries
placeholders.default: Menu.Play = Play; Menu.Settings = Settings; Menu.Quit = Quit to Desktop

presets.prompt:
Create `{{content_folder}}/Localization/{{table_name}}` with these entries: {{entries}}.
1. hyper_memory_recall "localization keys" for the project's key naming rule. hyper_project_search (kinds asset, query "ST_") for existing String Tables: if one already covers this screen, say so and add to it instead.
2. Epic's StringTableTools create, then set_entry per entry: keys exactly as given, source strings as written, no trailing spaces.
3. list_keys, and get_entry for each key; get_table_id and get_namespace.
4. hyper_data_inspect on the table (load it with AssetTools load_asset if it reports asset_not_loaded): its string_table record shows the same TableId and namespace. hyper_data_validate on the full Snapshot (marked incomplete by design: entries are read with StringTableTools).
5. Report a table: key | source string | PASS/FAIL; then the TableId to use with LOCTABLE("<TableId>", "<Key>") in C++ or as a text property's String Table reference in the editor. Leave it unsaved unless I ask.

presets.title: Set the project's default maps and game mode
presets.summary: Change the editor startup map, game default map and global game mode through Epic's config tools, prove the saved values and check the mode in play.
presets.prompt:
Set {{project}}'s Maps & Modes: editor startup map {{startup_map}}, game default map {{game_map}}, global default game mode {{game_mode}}.
1. hyper_project_search (kinds asset): each map and the game mode exist; stop on any that is missing.
2. Epic's ConfigSettingsToolset59: ListCategories for container Project, ListSections to find Maps & Modes, GetSectionSchema for its property names, then GetSectionPropertyValues for EditorStartupMap, GameDefaultMap and GlobalDefaultGameMode: the before values.
3. SetSectionProperties with only those three properties (it saves the section to the project's config).
4. GetSectionPropertyValues again: each equals what I asked for.
5. Read {{level}}'s World Settings DefaultGameMode with Epic's ObjectTools get_properties. If it has no override, hyper_verify_run, one case: AssertExists the game mode's class name (such as BP_MenuGameMode); otherwise say the level's override wins in play.
6. hyper_memory_remember the decision as type decision, titled with the fact itself (such as "The game starts in L_MainMenu with BP_MenuGameMode").
7. Report a table: setting | before | after | PASS/FAIL, then the play check, and name the config file that changed.

presets.title: Add states to a gameplay enum and recheck its users
presets.summary: Preview the enum change with HyperAI's data plan, append the new values, then compile every Blueprint that uses the enum and list switches to wire.
presets.prompt:
Append {{values}} to enum {{selected_asset}}; rename and remove nothing. If the blueprint_structure pack is unavailable, stop after step 2.
1. hyper_data_inspect on it (load it first with Epic's AssetTools load_asset if it reports asset_not_loaded): the current values in order and the PersistedFingerprint.
2. Preview: hyper_data_apply_plan with bDryRun true, TargetPath the enum, that fingerprint as ExpectedPersistedFingerprint, and one `user_enum.add_value` op per new value (Name, optional DisplayName); report Effects.AddCount. This plan only previews enum edits.
3. Apply: one hyper_blueprint_structure_apply_plan (fresh OperationId, bSave false) with `enum.add_value` (Asset the enum, Values {{values}}); hyper_operation_wait if it waits for approval.
4. hyper_data_inspect again and hyper_data_validate on the full Snapshot: old values kept in place, new ones appended.
5. hyper_asset_dependency_graph with direction referencers and maxDepth 1. Load each referencing Blueprint (AssetTools load_asset) and compile it with Epic's BlueprintTools compile_blueprint, which saves nothing; then hyper_blueprint_debug_inspect (0 errors) and hyper_blueprint_structure_inspect with bNodes and Find "Switch": list each Switch on this enum whose new pins are unwired (do not wire them).
6. Report a PASS/FAIL table: values before and after, each referencer's compile status, switches to wire. Leave the enum and the Blueprints unsaved unless I ask.

presets.title: Import a CSV of enemy stats into a DataTable
presets.summary: Import a CSV file into a DataTable on an existing row struct, check every column matched, and prove the row count and sample values.

placeholders.name: csv_path
placeholders.label: CSV file
placeholders.hint: Absolute path on disk; the first column holds the row names

presets.prompt:
Import `{{csv_path}}` as `{{content_folder}}/Data/{{table_name}}` with row struct `{{row_struct}}`.
1. Read the CSV's header and count its data rows (read only). Get the struct's fields: Epic's DataTableTools search_row_structs, or hyper_data_inspect on {{row_struct}} if it is a user-defined struct. Every CSV column after the first must match a field by name; list unmatched columns and stop if any field the game reads is missing.
2. hyper_data_inspect on {{content_folder}}/Data/{{table_name}}: it must report does_not_exist; otherwise stop and ask.
3. Epic's DataTableTools import_file into {{content_folder}}/Data with that schema.
4. hyper_data_inspect on the new table (load it with AssetTools load_asset if it reports asset_not_loaded) and hyper_data_validate on the full Snapshot: the row count equals the CSV's, and the row names match its first column.
5. get_rows for the first, middle and last rows: the values equal the CSV cells.
6. Report a PASS/FAIL table: columns matched, rows imported against the CSV, the 3 sample rows. Leave it unsaved unless I ask.

presets.title: Audit gameplay tags for unused and misspelled entries
presets.summary: List the project's gameplay tags with their referencers, flag unused tags, near-duplicates and naming breaks, and suggest removals for approval.
presets.prompt:
Audit {{project}}'s gameplay tags under `{{parent_tag}}`; remove or rename nothing.
1. hyper_memory_recall "gameplay tag naming" for the project's tag rules.
2. Epic's GameplayTagsToolset59: ListTags with parentTag {{parent_tag}}; for each tag, GetTagInfo (where it is defined) and FindReferencersByTag.
3. Flag tags with 0 referencers; near-duplicates (the same words in another case, plural and singular, typos one letter apart); tags that break the naming rule; and leaf tags placed directly under the root.
4. hyper_project_search (kinds cpp_symbol) for each unreferenced tag, since C++ (UE_DEFINE_GAMEPLAY_TAG, RequestGameplayTag) may use a tag without an asset reference.
5. Report a table: tag | source | referencers | C++ hits | PASS/WARN/FAIL | suggestion. RemoveTag and RenameTag change the whole project: list the ones you suggest, and run each only if I approve it by name.

presets.title: Make a Data Registry over the selected data tables
presets.summary: Build a Data Registry whose items come from the selected data tables (and a folder of more), check every id resolves, and say how to register it.

placeholders.name: type
placeholders.label: Registry type
placeholders.hint: The name every id starts with (Items:Sword).

placeholders.name: folder
placeholders.label: Folder of more tables
placeholders.hint: A folder whose matching tables join too (a meta source); empty for none.

presets.prompt:
Make a Data Registry over {{selected_assets}}. Follow the unreal-data-registry skill; if hyper_data_registry_apply_plan is not available, say the Data Registry plugin is off and stop.
1. Read the tables' row struct (Epic's DataTable tools or hyper_data_inspect); every table must share it.
2. hyper_data_registry_apply_plan with bDryRun true, Asset `{{content_folder}}/Data/DR_{{type}}`, Operations: create with RegistryType {{type}} and ItemStruct the row struct; one source.add data_table per selected table; if `{{folder}}` is not empty, a source.add data_table_meta with Paths [{{folder}}]. Read Sources and Warnings, then run it with bDryRun false and a fresh OperationId (hyper_operation_wait with bWaitThroughApproval true if it waits).
3. hyper_data_registry_inspect the registry: ItemCount, and whether it is in a scanned directory.
4. hyper_data_registry_lookup three item names from the tables.
Report the registry, its sources in order, item count, the three lookups, and if it is not scanned, the Project Settings > Game > Data Registry > Directories To Scan entry to add. Leave it unsaved.

presets.title: Check a Data Registry's sources and ids
presets.summary: Read the selected Data Registry's sources, the tables they resolve to, hidden ids, and whether the game loads it. Changes nothing.
presets.prompt:
Review the Data Registry {{selected_asset}}. Change nothing.
1. If hyper_data_registry_inspect is not available, the Data Registry plugin is off: say so and stop. hyper_data_registry_inspect with Asset {{selected_asset}}.
2. hyper_data_registry_lookup with the first ten item names, Format json.
Report a table with one row per source: kind, tables, items, PASS or the problem (a table whose rows do not match the item struct, a meta source that finds nothing). List ids that one source hides in another (Shadowed), and whether the registry is in Directories To Scan.

presets.title: Move a gameplay tag branch into its own tag source
presets.summary: Give one tag branch its own tag ini with Epic's GameplayTagsToolset59, move its tags there, add new ones, and prove nothing lost its referencers.
presets.prompt:
Put every tag under `{{branch}}` into its own tag source `{{source}}`, then add {{new_tags}} there. Change no other tags. Use Epic's `GameplayTagsToolset59.GameplayTagsToolset59`; if it is not listed, say so and stop. On this engine every argument of these toolsets is required: pass empty strings, 0 or null for the ones you do not need.
1. hyper_memory_recall "gameplay tag naming" for the project's tag rules; check each new tag against them.
2. ListTagSources and ListTagSourceRoots; ListTags with parentTag {{branch}}; GetTagInfo on each (its source) and FindReferencersByTag (count only).
3. If `{{source}}` does not exist, AddTagSource with sourceName {{source}} and tagRoot the first root ListTagSourceRoots gives.
4. MoveTags with the branch's tags that are not already there and targetTagSource {{source}}; read the result's moved and skipped lists. Tags defined in C++ or a DataTable cannot move: name them.
5. AddTag for each of {{new_tags}} with a one-line devComment and tagSource {{source}}.
6. ListTagsInSource {{source}}; GetTagInfo and FindReferencersByTag again for each moved tag. hyper_project_search (kinds cpp_symbol) for the branch name, for native tags.
Reply with a PASS/FAIL table, one row per tag: old source, new source, referencers before and after (unchanged), or why it stayed. Then the new tags with their sources.
